summary: Every confirmed WP9 finding is the same defect wearing different clothes: a standard-pipeline rewrite grants itself permission from *possible* binding names (or ignores names visible from an enclosing scope) where soundness requires *assured* names, or fails closed on an unrelated signal (jar CodeSource) instead of the declared contract. The fixes are four precise guards plus one contract flip, each independently landable and all small: (1) QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer may push a VALUES relation through a scoped BIND only if every Filter inside the pushed-into algebra has its pushed variables assured by that Filter's own argument (the review's whole-arg assured check is neither sufficient nor necessary); (2) FilterOptimizer.FilterRelocator may move a filter into one operand of Join/LeftJoin only if each filter variable is assured there or cannot be bound by the sibling operand (same rule for Extension element names), and PackedFilterRules:91-92 gets the identical mask rule via a new allocation-free `maskContainsAllIntersection` accessor; (3) ScalarEvaluationEffects becomes a denylist (VOLATILE iff `Function.mustReturnDifferentResult()`, Now QUERY_STABLE, unregistered UNKNOWN; model operators recognised by exact package, no CodeSource); (4) SameTermFilterOptimizer's EmptySet shortcut must count names visible from enclosing EXISTS bodies and LATERAL left arguments as possibly bound. A small shared `BindingScopeAnalysis` helper (roadmap 4.1) carries the two predicates (`canPushInto`, `outerVisibleNames`) so wp1/wp2 can adopt them. Of the two pre-existing compliance failures, LMDB `builtinFunction()[20]` is `SES869ValueOfNow` whose `p == n` identity assertion is broken because LmdbValueLookupOptimizer wraps the shared NOW literal into a fresh LmdbLiteral per ValueConstant (confirmed by code reading; fix is identity-memoised lookup, wp1 file); the four custom-aggregate DISTINCT failures are exactly the five GROUP BY tests that assert implementation-defined group order with no ORDER BY, the Group/DISTINCT code is unchanged vs develop, so the producer of the order change is not yet identified and a run-and-diff triage is specified rather than a fix. Item 3.11.6 is designed as a three-layer differential run (develop-vs-branch compliance id diff per store, operator-mode sweep forcing every EXISTS/LeftJoin/HashJoin alternative, and a seeded NoREC-style oracle generator against StrictEvaluationStrategy on unoptimized algebra).

findings.title: QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer pushes VALUES through a scope-changing BIND using possible names; nested Filters observe boundness of the pushed variable
findings.severity: S1 wrong results, REG vs develop (develop has no such push at all: git show origin/develop shows meet(Join) ends at the LeftJoin cases), all stores (LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline:257 also runs QUERY_MODEL_NORMALIZER)
findings.rootCause: /Users/havardottestad/Documents/Programming/rdf4j-small-things/core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer.java:102-118 rewrites Join(BSA, Extension[scope](A)) into Extension[scope](Join(BSA, A)). canPushAssignmentThroughScopedExtension (:127-147) checks only (a) the BIND expressions do not mention/assign the pushed names and (b) `extension.getArg().getBindingNames().containsAll(assignmentNames)` (:133), a *possible*-name check. isPlainJoinAlgebra (:149-164) admits any non-scoped Filter whose condition is not itself a SubQueryValueOperator (:159-161), so `Filter(!BOUND(?x), …)` and `Filter(Not(Exists(…?x…)), …)` pass. After the push the Join is evaluated as a bound (nested-loop) join, so the FilterIterator inside A sees ?x bound from the outer VALUES row, whereas the original plan evaluated A unbound (scope boundary) and joined afterwards. This is only equivalent when every Filter in A that mentions a pushed name has that name assured by the Filter's own argument (then the merged value equals the row's own value by join compatibility). In the repro `VALUES ?x {UNDEF}` inside GRAPH leaves ?x unassured, so `!BOUND(?x)` flips true→false (0 rows instead of 2) and `NOT EXISTS { ?s :q ?x }` flips false→true (spurious rows). Note the review's proposed fix `extension.getArg().getAssuredBindingNames().containsAll(assignmentNames)` is NOT sufficient: A = Join(Filter(!BOUND(?x), SP1), SP2(?x)) assures ?x at the top yet the Filter sits over SP1 where ?x is not assured, and bound evaluation still flips it. It is also stronger than needed (a filter-free A with unassured ?x is pushable).

findings.rootCause: /Users/havardottestad/Documents/Programming/rdf4j-small-things/core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/FilterOptimizer.java:349-367 meet(Join): `join.getLeftArg().getBindingNames().containsAll(filterVars)` (possible names) permits descending into the left operand. For `?s :p ?y OPTIONAL{?s :q ?x} ?s :r ?x FILTER(?x=?y)` the left operand LeftJoin has possible {s,y,x} so the relocator descends, meet(LeftJoin) (:378-384) finds the LeftJoin's left SP lacks x and relocates the filter onto the LeftJoin. Same pattern at meet(LeftJoin) :379 (`leftJoin.getLeftArg().getBindingNames()` — Filter(c, LeftJoin(L,R)) → LeftJoin(Filter(c,L),R) is wrong when c mentions a variable only possibly bound in L and possibly bound in R, e.g. two stacked OPTIONALs binding the same ?x) and at meet(Extension) :424 (does not check filterVars ∩ element names, and ExtensionIterator.setValue overwrites bindings unconditionally). The second repro `VALUES ?x {UNDEF :w} ?s :p ?x FILTER(sameTerm(?x,:v))` is the same defect: BSA possible {x} contains filterVars so the filter is pushed onto the BSA, whose UNDEF row then errors; the correct target is the SP (x assured there).

findings.title: SameTermFilterOptimizer's 'unbound variable -> EmptySet' shortcut ignores variables visible from enclosing scopes (EXISTS/NOT EXISTS bodies, LATERAL right arguments)
findings.severity: S1 wrong results, PRE (file identical to develop), all stores (standard pipeline and LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline:255 both run it)
findings.rootCause: /Users/havardottestad/Documents/Programming/rdf4j-small-things/core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/SameTermFilterOptimizer.java:83-90: `bindingNames = filterArg.getBindingNames()`; if a sameTerm operand Var without a value is not in that set the whole Filter is replaced by EmptySet. SameTermFilterVisitor is an AbstractSimpleQueryModelVisitor(false) so it descends into Exists subqueries; for `FILTER EXISTS { ?s :q ?o FILTER(sameTerm(?x, :v1)) }` the inner filterArg is SP(?s :q ?o), ?x is absent, and the EXISTS body becomes EmptySet, although SPARQL EXISTS substitutes the outer solution (?x is bound per probe). The same holds for a Filter inside the right argument of Lateral (model class exists: core/queryalgebra/model/.../Lateral.java; outer left bindings are visible). The inlining path (:92-97) is already correct: an outer-correlated variable is never assured by filterArg so nothing is inlined. Secondary latent issue (:118): the VALUES guard uses bsa.getAssuredBindingNames(); on this branch UNDEF rows revoke assurance, so a BSA that possibly binds the renamed variable escapes the guard and renameVar (:164-173) cannot rewrite BSA rows.
findings.fix:
Track outer-visible names while visiting. In SameTermFilterVisitor add `private final Deque<Set<String>> outerVisible = new ArrayDeque<>();` and:
- override `meetSubQueryValueOperator(SubQueryValueOperator node)`: compute `visible = new HashSet<>(outerVisible.isEmpty() ? Set.of() : outerVisible.peek()); QueryModelNode p = node.getParentNode(); while (p != null && !(p instanceof TupleExpr)) p = p.getParentNode(); if (p != null) visible.addAll(((TupleExpr) p).getBindingNames());` (for a Filter that is its arg's names; for a LeftJoin condition L∪R; for Extension/Order their arg — all conservative supersets), push, `super.meetSubQueryValueOperator(node)`, pop.
- override `meet(Lateral node)`: visit left arg normally; push `top ∪ node.getLeftArg().getBindingNames()` around visiting the right arg.
- in extracted(): `Set<String> possiblyBound = outerVisible.isEmpty() ? filterArg.getBindingNames() : union(filterArg.getBindingNames(), outerVisible.peek());` and use possiblyBound for the EmptySet shortcut (:84-90). Keep the assured check (:92-97) on filterArg only (never inline a correlated variable). Treat outer names as visible throughout the EXISTS body regardless of nested scope-change flags (EXISTS substitution is textual over the whole pattern), i.e. never produce EmptySet on that basis inside an EXISTS.
- (latent) change the BSA guard at :118 to `bsa.getBindingNames()` (possible names may only block).
Expose the ancestor walk as `BindingScopeAnalysis.outerVisibleNames(QueryModelNode)` so LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer (wp1, same blind spot per raw notes) can reuse it.

findings.fix:
Three layers, all read-only with respect to production code (Routine C), run per store class (Memory, Native, LMDB; ExtensibleStore/FedX optional):
1. Baseline parity: two worktrees (origin/develop 5eee576f5a and HEAD 4354ff137b), named Maven workspaces so they can run concurrently (`python3 .codex/skills/mvnf/scripts/mvnf.py --workspace dev compliance/sparql --retain-logs` / `--workspace br`), extract failing ids with `python3 scripts/agent-evidence.py` from the GAV-specific surefire dirs, diff per class (SPARQL11/12 Query+Update, RepositorySPARQLComplianceTestSuite subclasses incl. optional(), lateral(), filterScopeTests(), aggregate(), arbitraryLengthPath()). Precondition for LMDB: the three 3.9 NPEs (LmdbPipelinePlanCache$DatasetIdentity.immutable:502, $2.meet:430, PatternKeys.predicateKey:36) mask 41 tests — fix or exclude them first, otherwise LMDB parity is uninformative.
2. Operator-mode sweep on the branch (roadmap 4.8 'every alternative chosen at least once'): rerun the Memory compliance classes under each forced configuration: (a) a test-only QueryOptimizer appended to the pipeline via a custom EvaluationStrategyFactory in newRepository() that stamps `filter.setStringMetricPlanned(OPTIMIZER_FILTER_ALGORITHM_HINT, mode)` on every Filter whose condition contains Exists, for mode in {streaming-correlated, memoized-correlated, materialized-hash, default}; (b) `-Drdf4j.evaluation.semiAntiMemoCapacity=1`; (c) `-D…leftjoin.maxMaterializedRightRows=1`, `-D…leftjoin.memoized.maxKeys=1`, `-D…leftjoin.memoized.maxRows=1` (force spill/fallback); (d) if MaterializedExistsFilterIteration.PROBE_LIMIT / MaterializationCache has a switch, its smallest value. Any id failing in one mode but not another is a mode-specific executor bug (file to wp4 with a 2-5 triple repro).
3. Oracle differential (NoREC/TLP-style, seeded): a generator test in core/queryalgebra/evaluation modelled on SPARQLMinusIterationFuzzTest (fixed seeds) and PackedRuleSemanticsReviewReproTest.evaluate (StrictEvaluationStrategy over the *unoptimized* algebra as reference): random 2-5-triple datasets with mixed literal forms ("1"^^int, "01"^^int, 1.0, "a"@en/@EN, UNDEF VALUES) and random shapes over OPTIONAL (with/without condition, over sub-SELECT with LIMIT/aggregate), MINUS (inside OPTIONAL, with right-only filter), EXISTS/NOT EXISTS (over sub-SELECT, UNION body, inside a joined group — the f5 shapes), VALUES with UNDEF, paths :p* :p+ :p? and zero-length with constants on cyclic data, LATERAL; compare bags against (i) the standard pipeline on MemoryStore and (ii) LmdbStore (lmdb module). Optional third oracle: Jena ARQ via the existing ThemeQueryCatalogJenaOracleTest pattern (testsuites/benchmark-common). Deliverable: per-store, per-mode failing-id diff plus one minimal red test per divergence handed to the owning WP.

findings.title: LMDB builtinFunction()[20] = SES869ValueOfNow: NOW() shared literal loses object identity through LmdbValueLookupOptimizer
findings.severity: S3 (equal values, broken identity contract asserted by the testsuite) unless the run shows assertEquals failing too; PRE on the branch; LMDB only
findings.rootCause: Dynamic test #20 (1-based) of BuiltinFunctionTest.tests() (/Users/havardottestad/Documents/Programming/rdf4j-small-things/testsuites/sparql/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/testsuite/sparql/tests/BuiltinFunctionTest.java:427-449) is SES869ValueOfNow (:110-127): `SELECT ?p (NOW() as ?n) { BIND(NOW() as ?p) }` asserting `assertEquals(p, n)` AND `assertTrue(p == n)`. On every store ConstantOptimizer (:280-300, isConstantZeroArgFunction) folds both NOW() calls into ValueConstants holding DefaultEvaluationStrategy.sharedValueOfNow (:218, reset per QueryRoot :370/:420/:1098), one Literal instance. The LMDB pipeline then runs LmdbValueLookupOptimizer (/Users/havardottestad/Documents/Programming/rdf4j-small-things/core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbValueLookupOptimizer.java:69-71 meet(ValueConstant) -> `node.setValue(lookup(node.getValue()).value)`; lookup :116-132 -> `valueStore.getLmdbValue(value)` creates a fresh LmdbLiteral wrapper per call, id UNKNOWN). Each ValueConstant therefore ends up with a distinct but equal LmdbLiteral, so `p == n` is false while `assertEquals` passes. Memory/Native have no such step and pass.
findings.fix: In LmdbValueLookupOptimizer keep an `IdentityHashMap<Value, Lookup>` for the duration of one optimize() pass and return the memoised Lookup for the same input instance (also de-duplicates repeated constants and ValueStore round-trips). Alternative (less preferred): return the original Value when `id == UNKNOWN_ID` — rejected because the unknown-id LmdbValue is used as a 'not in store' marker (knownValue == null) by later rewrites. File is owned by wp1 (Lmdb*Optimizer); land as a tiny wp1 change or with wp1's approval.

files.change: per-pass IdentityHashMap<Value, Lookup> memo in lookup(); ValueConstants/Vars holding the same Value instance resolve to the same LmdbValue instance

findings.risk: Low. Identity is only strengthened; memo lives for one optimize() call.
findings.recommendationReason: Mechanism is clear from code and the fix is a few lines; it also removes redundant ValueStore lookups. Confirm the exact failing assertion by running LmdbSPARQLComplianceTest builtinFunction first (rule: in-repo red test before the change; the compliance test is already red).

sharedInfrastructure: New package-private/static helper in core/queryalgebra/evaluation, org.eclipse.rdf4j.query.algebra.evaluation.optimizer.BindingScopeAnalysis (roadmap 4.1: one binding/scope analysis, 'rules that introduce or move predicates require assured; possible names may only block'). Methods: (1) `boolean canPushInto(Set<String> filterVars, TupleExpr target, TupleExpr sibling)` = target possible ⊇ filterVars AND ∀v∈filterVars: v ∈ assured(target) ∨ v ∉ possible(sibling) — used by FilterOptimizer.meet(Join)/meet(LeftJoin) (3.11.2) and mirrored bit-for-bit in PackedFilterRules via maskContainsAll + maskContainsAllIntersection (3.2.5); (2) `boolean filterDependsOnlyOnAssured(Filter f, Set<String> names)` = VarNameCollector(f.condition) ∩ names ⊆ assured(f.arg) — used by QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer (3.11.1); (3) `Set<String> outerVisibleNames(QueryModelNode n)` = union over enclosing SubQueryValueOperator boundaries of the nearest enclosing TupleExpr's possible names, plus Lateral left-arg names when n sits in a Lateral right arg — used by SameTermFilterOptimizer (3.11.4). Candidates to adopt it: wp1 LmdbBoundSimplifierOptimizer (BOUND(?x)->false inside EXISTS, same blind spot), LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.makeOptionalBindingMandatory (uses right-arg possible names), LmdbNullRejectingOptionalSupport; wp2 PackedLogicalRuleProgram MINUS->NOT EXISTS guard and addScalarDependencies (referenced-vs-output).
